article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: Baby Gluey × Cinderella 99
Breeder: MrSoul / Brothers Grimm Seeds
THC Content: 27-30%
CBD Content: Typically low
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , pinene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Cedarwood, earth, pine, Chem fuel
Flowering Time (Indoor): 63–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid October
Indoor Yield: Heavy
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Grimm Glue takes the sticky, heavily resinous personality associated with Glue-family marijuana and pulls it in a noticeably brighter direction. Instead of building the entire experience around body weight and raw fuel, Brothers Grimm Seeds introduced Cinderella 99 to a selected clone called Baby Gluey, creating cannabis with cedarwood, pine, earth, Chem-like pungency, Skunk, and occasional citrus layered into a remarkably resin-rich flower. The aroma can feel almost architectural: dry wood and evergreen appear first, then sharper glue, fuel, spice, and earthy funk emerge once the buds are broken apart. Mature flowers become exceptionally tacky, and the cultivar has earned a particularly strong following among growers producing rosin, bubble hash, and other concentrates.

The breeding goal was equally specific on the effects side. Baby Gluey impressed MrSoul with stability, yield, and extraordinary resin production, but its experience leaned heavier and sleepier than he wanted. Cinderella 99 was used to introduce more sparkle, mental energy, and complexity without losing the Glue characteristics that made the mother valuable. The finished hybrid can therefore begin with a lively, giggly cerebral rise before settling into a calmer physical state. With some growers reaching around 30% THC or higher, Grimm Glue combines old-school Chem-and-Skunk intensity with the energetic personality of one of Brothers Grimm’s most famous creations.
Genetics and Lineage

The original cross is Baby Gluey × Cinderella 99. Baby Gluey was a clone Brothers Grimm evaluated for roughly a year before deciding it deserved a place in the breeding program. MrSoul specifically valued the plant because it resisted intersex expression under stress, yielded well, and produced exceptional resin. The breeder has not published a complete formal pedigree for Baby Gluey, so attaching an invented modern strain tree to the clone would be misleading. What is documented is its Glue heritage, including the Chemdog-and-Skunk character that appears clearly in the finished flower.

Cinderella 99 provides the far better documented half of the pedigree. MrSoul created C99 from Princess, a remarkable female grown from a seed found in Jack Herer flower purchased in Amsterdam. Princess was compact, resinous, fast flowering, pineapple-scented, and strongly cerebral despite its manageable indoor structure. MrSoul then used a cubing process, beginning with pollen from a resinous Shiva Skunk male and repeatedly backcrossing selected descendants to Princess. The P94 generation represented roughly 15/16 Princess genetics, and Princess × P94 produced the finished Cinderella 99 line.

For Grimm Glue, Brothers Grimm reversed a favorite C99 female using STS so that it could provide feminized pollen to Baby Gluey. This was not simply a potency cross. Cinderella 99 was chosen specifically to lift the mother’s heavier personality, contribute stronger mental animation, and maintain fast, vigorous growth. The result preserves Glue-style resin and Chem/Skunk pungency while adding a more energetic and playful quality than the Baby Gluey mother expressed on its own.
Effects and Experience

The cerebral phase is usually the first clear departure from traditional Glue-family expectations. Rather than beginning with immediate heaviness, the high can arrive as a bright, buoyant shift in mood. Laughter may come more easily, conversation becomes more animated, and music or creative activities can feel unusually engaging. Brothers Grimm has described the experience as sparkling and giggly, which captures the way Cinderella 99 changes the otherwise weightier personality inherited from Baby Gluey.

Physical relaxation develops later and tends to feel steadier than abrupt. Shoulders loosen, the body becomes more settled, and the initial mental intensity gradually loses some of its sharpness without disappearing entirely. Moderate consumption can preserve a surprisingly functional balance between creative stimulation and bodily ease. Gaming, drawing, making music, watching a movie, or spending an evening with friends can all fit comfortably into this stage because the cultivar does not automatically push the session toward sleep.

Potency can be substantial. Brothers Grimm identifies Grimm Glue as one of its highest-THC offerings, and growers have produced flower around 30% and even into the low 30s. At that strength, excessive consumption can turn an enjoyable cerebral lift into racing thoughts, dizziness, dry mouth, dry eyes, or temporary anxiety. Larger servings may also allow the Glue side to assert itself more strongly, producing a heavier and increasingly sedentary finish. Careful dosing preserves the cultivar’s most distinctive trait: the movement from animated euphoria into comfortable physical relaxation.
Medical Benefits

Grimm Glue may appeal to medical cannabis consumers seeking substantial THC potency without an immediately sedating onset. The combination of mental elevation and later body relaxation can be relevant when stress and physical tension appear together. Some consumers may find that the brighter early phase makes persistent discomfort less mentally consuming, while the later effects soften muscular tension and encourage a slower pace. THC influences pain perception, mood, appetite, and sensory processing through several neurological pathways, although responses vary greatly from person to person.

Myrcene, pinene, and beta-caryophyllene are the breeder-listed dominant terpenes. Myrcene contributes earthy and herbal depth, pinene reinforces the fresh resinous and evergreen character, and caryophyllene adds peppery spice while interacting with CB2 cannabinoid receptors. These compounds help explain the cultivar’s aroma and may influence the overall experience, but they should not be treated as individual medical treatments. Patients using high-THC weed should consider tolerance, medication interactions, and the cannabinoid analysis of the specific harvest rather than relying solely on a strain name.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Cedarwood is one of Grimm Glue’s most distinctive aromatic signatures. Instead of the sweet fruit or dessert scent that dominates much contemporary marijuana, cured flowers can smell dry, woody, earthy, and almost freshly cut, with pine resin adding a crisp evergreen edge. Break the bud open and the Glue ancestry becomes louder: Chem-like fuel, Skunk, pungent earth, and adhesive-style funk rise behind the wood.

Myrcene helps deepen the earthy base, while pinene sharpens the forest-like character. Beta-caryophyllene supplies pepper, wood, and spice, creating a terpene profile that feels savory rather than confectionery. Depending on phenotype and curing, a mild citrus note may appear behind the heavier aromas, likely reflecting some of the brighter character associated with Cinderella 99. The overall bouquet is complex without relying on sweetness.

Flavor tends to begin with cedar and pine before shifting toward Chem, Skunk, and earth during the exhale. Peppery spice can linger afterward, occasionally joined by mild citrus or fruit. Vaporization exposes the woody and evergreen details particularly well, whereas combustion tends to emphasize Glue-family pungency. A slow dry and controlled cure are valuable because harsh processing can flatten the cedarwood character and leave little beyond generic gas and earth.
Growing Information

Grimm Glue is a vigorous photoperiod plant that can gain substantial size during vegetative growth and early flower. Brothers Grimm recommends taking advantage of its natural structure rather than forcing excessive manipulation. Lower and weak interior branches can be pruned so that the plant concentrates energy into larger upper colas. Growers who prefer a broader canopy can still use topping and low-stress training, while SOG and SCROG systems are both practical choices for indoor production.

The current breeder flowering window is approximately 63–70 days. During the later weeks, bud weight becomes one of the most important practical considerations. Flowers can become large, dense, and exceptionally resinous, and unsupported branches may bend under the load. Stakes or trellising should be installed before the plants become difficult to handle. Brothers Grimm consistently describes Grimm Glue as a heavy-yielding marijuana variety rather than publishing one fixed grams-per-square-meter number, which is more realistic because final production depends on light intensity, plant count, canopy size, root volume, and vegetative duration.

Environmental control becomes especially important once the colas gain density. Consistent airflow and moderate late-flower humidity help prevent moisture from remaining inside thick flowers. Feeding can be generous when plants are healthy, but root-zone stability matters more than simply increasing fertilizer concentration. One of the breeder’s strongest endorsements of the cultivar is its extraction performance: Grimm Glue is repeatedly recommended for rosin and bubble hash, reflecting the abundant resin inherited from Baby Gluey and reinforced through selection.

Outdoor plants can become large, productive specimens when given a full season. Brothers Grimm specifically recommends Grimm Glue for outdoor and greenhouse production, and its vigorous branching responds well to early structural training. In many suitable Northern Hemisphere gardens, a 63–70 day bloom places maturity around early to mid-October, although latitude, planting date, and local photoperiod can move that window.

Strong outdoor support becomes just as important as it is indoors. Heavy branches exposed to wind or rain can split once the flowers reach full size, making stakes, cages, or trellises worthwhile before autumn. Growers in humid areas should also keep the interior canopy open so air can move through the plant. When strong sunlight, root space, irrigation, and dry finishing weather cooperate, Grimm Glue can produce both considerable flower weight and the heavy trichome coverage that has made it a favorite among solventless extractors.
FAQ
What strains make Grimm Glue?

Grimm Glue was created by MrSoul of Brothers Grimm Seeds from Baby Gluey crossed with Cinderella 99. Baby Gluey is a selected Glue-family clone valued for stability, yield, heavy resin, and Chem/Skunk character. Cinderella 99 is MrSoul’s famous Princess × P94 line, created through a multi-generation cubing process.
Is Grimm Glue indica or sativa?

The cultivar is best described as a balanced hybrid. Baby Gluey contributes a heavier, more relaxing personality, while Cinderella 99 adds a much brighter and more energetic cerebral component. The high commonly begins upbeat and giggly before physical relaxation becomes more noticeable.
How much THC is in Grimm Glue?

Brothers Grimm describes Grimm Glue as its highest-THC bulk strain and notes that some growers reach approximately 30% THC. Individual grower tests have also exceeded that level. Actual potency depends on phenotype, lighting, cultivation, harvest maturity, curing, storage, and laboratory methodology.
What does Grimm Glue taste like?

Cedarwood, pine, earth, Chem fuel, Skunk, peppery spice, and mild citrus make up the core profile. The woody cedar quality is particularly distinctive, while the exhale tends to reveal more of the pungent Glue ancestry. Myrcene, pinene, and beta-caryophyllene are the breeder-listed dominant terpenes.
How long does Grimm Glue take to flower?

The current Brothers Grimm flowering recommendation is approximately 63–70 days. Plants produce large, heavy colas and should be supported with stakes or trellising during bloom. Outdoors, that flowering duration generally translates to an early- to mid-October harvest in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates.
Final Thoughts on Grimm Glue

Grimm Glue demonstrates how thoughtful breeding can alter the personality of a famous genetic family without erasing the traits that made it valuable. Baby Gluey supplied extraordinary resin, strong yield, stability, and classic Chem/Skunk pungency, but its effects leaned heavier than MrSoul wanted. Cinderella 99 introduced the missing contrast: mental energy, laughter, creative stimulation, and the lively character that has defined C99 for decades.

The combination also works exceptionally well in the grow room. Plants are vigorous, flowering finishes in approximately 63–70 days, and the branches can become so heavily loaded that structural support is part of basic cultivation rather than an optional extra. Resin production is among the cultivar’s defining strengths, explaining why Brothers Grimm regularly recommends it for rosin, bubble hash, and other concentrate applications.

What separates Grimm Glue from countless Glue crosses is its cedarwood-and-pine identity and the unusual balance of effects. Chem fuel, Skunk, earth, and resin remain unmistakably present, yet the experience can feel brighter, more humorous, and more creative than the name implies. Potency around 30% in well-grown flower ensures that the strain never lacks intensity, but raw strength is not its most interesting feature.

For growers who want heavy yields and extraction-grade resin, or consumers who enjoy Glue genetics but prefer a more animated cerebral beginning, Grimm Glue occupies a particularly useful middle ground. It preserves the sticky, pungent foundation of its mother while allowing Cinderella 99 to reshape the high—and in doing so, it creates a cultivar that feels distinctly like Brothers Grimm rather than simply another variation on Glue.
